head.citation-title: Waste biomolecule-based carbonation of high-calcium byproduct to produce supplementary cementitious materials
head.abstracts: © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.Utilizing calcium-rich waste to enhance construction materials through carbon capture is an effective approach to mitigate carbon footprints and preserve the environment. In this study, waste high-calcium fly ash (HCFA) and calcium hydroxide powder (CH/CKD), a major component of waste cement kiln dust, were carbonated in the presence of tannic acid (TA). The effects of factors such as TA concentration, liquid-solid ratio, percentages of wastes, and compatibility of superplasticizers were examined. Carbonation occurred in two steps: first, calcium was leached from HCFA using tannic acid (TA); then, the pre-treated solution was carbonated with CO2. The resulting carbonated materials replaced cement in the mortar at 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% replacements. Compressive strength tests were conducted on 3, 7, and 28 days. Pretreating 40% HCFA with 0.05% TA improved both carbonation quality and mechanical strength of mortar (up to 25.5%) and also enhanced sustainability (cement reduction up to 40% along with higher carbon capture potential). The mix compositions were ranked by the multidimensional criteria of the decision-making technique, TOPSIS. Isothermal calorimetry, TGA, FTIR, XRD, and SEM imaging were performed for micro-characterization. TA-regulated carbonation allows high volume replacement of carbonated HCFA (up to 50%) by controlling CaCO3 polymorphs, thus refining microstructure and particle packing.
